Applicants: The table says "Manufacturer: Dibal S.A., Astintze Kalea, 26 - Pol. Ind. Neinver, 48160 Derio, Vizcaya, Spain". There's no separate applicant listed. Hmm. In NMi certs, typically the manufacturer is the applicant. The schema says manufacturers[] with name and address_lines. The table row is labeled "Manufacturer". I'll include it under manufacturers. Should applicants be included? The cert doesn't explicitly list an applicant. Rule 8: don't fabricate. But often manufacturer = applicant. I'll include manufacturers only, since the label says "Manufacturer". Actually, could put the same under applicants too since NMi typically means applicant. But to be safe, only manufacturers.

Certified type:
- Category: Non-automatic weighing instrument → canonical category... The schema examples list "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system"... For NWI, "Non-automatic weighing instrument". Page 2 mentions "Indicator:" for test reports. The certified type is "A Non-automatic weighing instrument", Type: NGDPOS. The category could be "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- type_designations: ["NGDPOS"]
- module_designation: The instrument is an indicator-based? Actually the certified type is a weighing instrument. The test reports include "Indicator" reports and "Load cells" reports (L6D and LAB). Should I record components? The cert names load cells L6D and LAB as sub-assemblies. Rule 6: components for complex instruments. The load cells are components: L6D and LAB load cells. I could add components:
  - role: "load cell", type_designations: ["L6D"]
  - role: "load cell", type_designations: ["LAB"]
  - role: "indicator" — the test reports say "Indicator" — the instrument NGDPOS is presumably an indicator? Actually NGDPOS is the type of the weighing instrument. The reports for "Indicator" suggest the certified type is an indicator used in weighing instruments. Hmm, "Identification of the certified type: A Non-automatic weighing instrument, Type: NGDPOS". Dibal makes retail scales (NGDPOS is a POS scale). The test reports are grouped under "Indicator:" and "Load cells:". So the instrument consists of an indicator (NGDPOS?) plus load cells L6D and LAB.

I'll include components for the load cells: role "load cell", type_designations ["L6D"] and ["LAB"], alternatives maybe "OR" since "Added L6D and LAB… loadcells" — they're alternative load cells presumably. Actually "L6D" and "LAB" could both be used. I'd say alternatives: "OR" is plausible but not stated. I'll leave alternatives null or omit. Hmm, "Added L6D and LAB… loadcells" — revision 2 added both. Typically a certificate lists multiple load cell types as alternatives. But I shouldn't fabricate; I'll leave alternatives null.

Characteristics (type_level):
- accuracy_class: "(III) or (IIII)" → value string "III or IIII"? The value is a string. unit null. I'll use value: "III or IIII" or "(III) or (IIII)". Keep as string "III, IIII"? I'll do "III or IIII".
- verification_scale_interval: e ≥ 2 g → value {min: 2, max: null}, unit "g"
- weighing_ranges: value types: single interval or multiple range → string? This is more of an attribute with list. Maybe "weighing_range_types": ["single interval", "multiple range"]? The schema expects structured values. I could record as value string "Single interval or Multiple range". Hmm. Better: characteristic "weighing_ranges" value: "Single interval or multiple range". Or two separate: I'll record as value string.
- max_scale_intervals_one_range: n ≤ 3000 → value {min: null, max: 3000}
- max_scale_intervals_multiple_range: 3000 per weighing range → {min:null, max:3000}
- max_number_of_weighing_ranges: 2
- temperature_range: -10 °C / 40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- power supply: "5 V DC (DPOS Format), or 12 V DC (G Format). 6 V DC (G Format battery) (not suitable for a road vehicle power supply)". This is config-dependent. Options:
  - power_supply_voltage config_level with axis "format": conditions "DPOS Format" 5 V, "G Format" 12 V, "G Format battery" 6 V.
  - Or type_level with a list. Rule: config axes vary by configuration → config_level. I'll do config_level:
    - attribute: power_supply_voltage, axis: "power_supply_configuration", values: [{condition: "DPOS Format", value: 5, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "G Format", value: 12, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "G Format (battery)", value: 6, unit_symbol: "V"}]
  - Also power_supply_type: "DC" and a note "not suitable for road vehicle power supply" — could be a type_level note: road_vehicle_power_supply_suitable: false. I'll add power_supply_type: DC. Maybe add "suitable_for_road_vehicle_power_supply": false as a note? Rule 8 — it's stated, so it's fine. I'll include "road_vehicle_power_supply" with value false? Might be overkill; keep it simple: power_supply_type "DC". And note in description? There's no description field for characteristics. I could add footnote-like text. I'll skip or include as boolean characteristic "suitable_for_road_vehicle_power_supply": false. I'll include it as it's meaningful.

- application: "Intended to be used for direct sales to the public" → application: "direct sales to the public"
- software_identification: "V-1.00"

Software notes: "The identification number will be displayed at start-up; the indicator has embedded software." Could be description fields. The schema doesn't have a place except maybe description in certified_type. I could omit or add to certified_type description. There's a description field: "free-text description if present". Not really present. I'll skip.

Test reports:
- Indicator reports: NMi-3968614-01..04 and NMi-4050268-01..04. These are type evaluation reports? Roles: they are the associated reports of tests and examinations → "type_evaluation_report" seems appropriate. The load cell ones (L6D: NMi-10200947-07, -08; LAB: R60/2000-NL1-10.07, NMi-12200582-01, NMi-3534839-01) are load cell certificates/test reports → role "test_report"? They're referenced load cell evaluation reports. I'll mark indicator ones as "type_evaluation_report" and load cell ones as "test_report". Hmm, or all as "test_report". The schema role enum: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. I'll use type_evaluation_report for the indicator ones (the instrument's own evaluation) and test_report for load cell ones (supporting evidence). Actually they may be load cell certificates of conformity... The LAB one "R60/2000-NL1-10.07" is an R60 certificate number. But these are listed as "reports". I'll use role "test_report" for load cells.

Verification scale interval: e ≥ 2 g → min 2.

Now the weighing_ranges characteristic: value could be "Single interval or Multiple range" — string. I'll do weighing_range_types with value string. Actually maybe two characteristics:
- weighing_ranges: {value: "Single interval or Multiple range"}

Max scale intervals: label canonical: "max_number_of_scale_intervals_one_weighing_range" and "max_number_of_scale_intervals_multiple_range". Values {min:null, max:3000}. The multiple-range one has note "(per weighing range)".

max_number_of_weighing_ranges: 2.

I'll include power_supply_type: {value: "DC"} at type level, and note not suitable for road vehicle power supply as characteristic "suitable_for_road_vehicle_power_supply": false? Hmm, the value false — schema says value can be number, range object, or string. Boolean not listed. I'll make it a string "false"? Or just skip. I could include a footnote-ish description. I'll skip the boolean, or include as note in description of the config? Keep it simple: skip. Actually, I think capturing it is valuable: "road_vehicle_power_supply": {value: "not suitable"} — awkward. I'll skip.

Components: load cells L6D and LAB. Include role "load cell". Alternatives: "OR"? The cert lists both L6D and LAB groups; typically the instrument may use either. Hmm, should I also add a component for the indicator? The test report section header "Indicator:" suggests the certified type is an indicator. But the certified type is described as a weighing instrument. I'll not add an indicator component.
